picks.title: Supermetrics lets Claude build ad campaigns on 6 platforms, paused by default
picks.rationale: New release: an AI assistant now drafts live campaigns across six ad platforms with a human-approval default, which changes who signs off on ad spend.
picks.excerpt: More than 6,000 customers have used the connector since February, active users up 250% a month on average. Who signs off before AI-drafted ads spend money?

picks.title: Ad Tech Briefing: Google's AI-reckoning
picks.rationale: The one pick from the 'AI search squeezing Google ad revenue' cluster: AI search draws more queries but earns less ad revenue per query than classic search, which matters for search budgets.
picks.excerpt: More people are searching, but Google’s AI-driven search experiences aren’t yet generating ad revenue at the same rate as conventional search.

picks.title: 3 AI Models Shopped Shopify’s Catalog – Each Picked A Different Winner
picks.rationale: Original experiment (1,980 runs) showing which product-data signals decide what AI shopping agents choose to buy, so merchants can act on it directly.
picks.excerpt: Three Claude models picked from the same 20 Shopify products 1,980 times and never agreed on the top product. Here is what decided their picks.

picks.title: Google tells advertisers AI search queries now run 3x longer
picks.rationale: Google's own advertiser briefing: AI search makes queries 3x longer and one in six multimodal, which changes how keyword and asset strategies should be built. The card should flag which figures lack a baseline.
picks.excerpt: One in six searches is multimodal, Google's Shivani Mohan told advertisers. Google's May data limited that to US AI Mode. Which other figures lack a baseline?

picks.title: AI recommendations are leading to returns
picks.rationale: New report linking AI product recommendations to higher returns and tracing the cause to bad product-description data, which retailers selling through AI channels can fix.
picks.excerpt: The problem may not have to do with the technology itself, but rather the product description data, according to a new report.
